reasons: Direction is correct: Corio is our party (licensee/hosting customer) and the carve-out in 13.5 gives Commerce One (vendor) ownership of Developments created solely by Corio, with no licence back — an effective transfer of our IP to the vendor, which is walk-away territory and fails the fallback (no perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free right to use/modify what we created).

Correctly classified as a deviation rather than an acceptable fallback: vendor ownership of Corio-created interface code with no licence-back is a material failure, not a mere shortfall from preferred wording.

Redline is substantively minimal and coherent across the mid-sentence paragraph break: p0115 now ends 'shall be owned by Corio.' and p0116 drops the orphaned 'intellectual property rights in the Developments.', leaving Commerce One's pre-existing materials and the Software untouched. The failed changed-character ratio checks are advisory and not borne out by the rendered text, which preserves all other language verbatim.
Comment is accurate, concise, in the required voice, cites the playbook position, and offers a sensible fallback (a support licence to Commerce One instead of ownership).

Omission of a Customer Data ownership sentence and the unresolved ownership of Software enhancements are correctly noted in the rationale as lesser drafting points rather than double-flagged; the core walk-away issue is fully remedied.
